name: Centar
tagline: The main square, the pedestrian streets and the kafana alley
description: Nis's core around Trg Kralja Milana and the pedestrianised Obrenoviceva, with the coppersmiths' alley of Kazandzijsko Sokace running off it, full of kafanas and bars. Everything the city offers socially is inside a few hundred metres, and the fortress is a short walk across the river.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the bars, restaurants and the fortress all within a five-minute walk
pros: The whole nightlife of the city on the doorstep
All bus lines and services converge here
cons: Loud on weekend nights, particularly in the alley
Highest rents in the city, though still low

name: Tvrdjava and Beograd Mala
tagline: The fortress side of the river, quieter and green
description: The north bank around the Ottoman fortress, whose grounds function as the city's central park, and the older low-rise streets of Beograd Mala behind it. It is a few minutes on foot across the bridge to the centre, but the atmosphere is entirely different: trees, walls and considerably less traffic.
bestFor: People who want the fortress park as their back garden and the centre over the bridge
pros: Fortress grounds for running and walking
Five minutes across the bridge to the centre
cons: Older housing stock in variable condition
Fewer shops and services than the centre
Events in the fortress bring noise in summer

name: Medijana
tagline: The main residential district, blocks and everyday life
description: The largest residential area of the city, east of the centre, built as blocks with markets, schools, clinics and the bus links to match. This is where most of Nis lives and where the rents are lowest for a decent flat. It is a fifteen-minute walk or a short bus ride to the square.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a normal local neighbourhood at the lowest cost
pros: Lowest rents for a decent-sized flat
Fifteen minutes on foot to the centre
cons: Limited cafes and no nightlife of its own
Pavements and public space are poorly maintained

name: Palilula
tagline: South of the centre, mixed streets and cheap rents
description: A large district south of the river taking in older houses, blocks and the approaches to the southern edge of the city. It is mixed in character and quality street by street, but the rents are very low and the centre is a walk or a short bus away. The Nisava path runs along its northern edge.
bestFor: Budget stays willing to look at a few flats before choosing a street
pros: Very low rents across the district
River path along the northern edge
Short bus ride or twenty-minute walk to the centre
cons: Quality varies considerably street to street
Little in the way of cafes or restaurants

name: Niska Banja
tagline: The spa suburb at the foot of Suva Planina
description: A spa settlement about ten kilometres east of the centre, built around thermal springs at the foot of the Suva Planina ridge. It has sanatoria, hotels, a park and a genuinely different pace, with hiking starting more or less at the edge of the village. Buses run into the city regularly.
bestFor: Stays built around walking and thermal water, with the city kept at arm's length
pros: Hiking on Suva Planina starts here
Thermal baths and a spa park
Very quiet and noticeably cleaner air
cons: Twenty-five minutes by bus to the centre
Older visitor demographic, little going on at night
